newsitem.title: USA: Glickman sees filling USDA vacancies this month.
newsitem.headline: Glickman sees filling USDA vacancies this month.

text.p: Agriculture Secretary Dan Glickman, who has lost four of his six undersecretaries, said Friday he hoped to begin filling the vacancies by the end of this month.

There will be no loss of momentum in the interim, he said, in major initiatives such as implementing a new meat inspection system and modernizing school lunches. In both of those areas, an undersecretary has resigned in recent weeks.
"The entire (Agriculture Department) team had a lot to do with that and that entire team will continue to have a lot to do with it," Glickman said.
Earlier this week, two consumer groups said they feared the meat inspection and school lunch reforms might falter due to the upcoming change in leadership.
Besides the food safety and public nutrition slots, the undersecretary posts that control agricultural research and the farm subsidy and export programs also are vacant.
"I hope you will know those names by the end of the month," Glickman said.
Glickman hinted that acting undersecretary Catherine Woteki, who oversees ag research, would continue in the job.
Glickman, Woteki and Undersecretary Jill Long, who oversees rural development portfolio, appeared at a news conference on how to apportion the $100 million Fund for Rural America.

Long could stay at the Agriculture Department through President Clinton's second term "if she wants," Glickman said. He did not comment on her possible role. Long and several others have been mentioned as candidates to head farm programs.
"Obviously, we have been talking to them (the White House) about names (of potential nominees)," Glickman said. "It's the president who nominates. I don't."
